2. Briefly stated the case of the petitioners in both the cases are as follows:
 That on 23.10.2021 at about 9.30 a.m. to 10.30 a.m.,
the petitioner in MVC No.5330/2021 was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA13-S-7770 along with the petitioner in MVC No.5331/2021 as a pillion rider near Sapotathota, Bhoopasandra main road, Bengaluru and Mohan Babu.

As a result, the rider of the Honda Deo died on the spot and the petitioners of these petitions fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately thereafter, the petitioners were shifted to Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital,

A case was registered  SCCH-1 MVC No.5330/2021 c/w  4 5331/2021 against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04- MT-6670 in Cr.No.79/2021 by the R.T.Nagar Traffic Police for the offences under Sections 279,337 and 304(A) of IPC.
Hence, these petitions are filed for compensation.

3. In response to the notice of the petitions, the respondents No.1 and 2 in both the cases have appeared before the Court through their respective counsels and have filed their written statement separately.
The respondent No.1 in both the cases has denied the entire averments of the petition as false.

The car bearing registration  SCCH-1 MVC No.5330/2021 c/w  5 5331/2021 No.KA-04-MT-6670 was insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The occurrence of the accident was intimated to the insurance company as per Section 134(c) of M.V.Act.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and excessive.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the petition averments as false.

The petitioners in order to prove their case have placed their oral evidence and documentary evidence as per Exs.P.1 to P.8, P.13, P.23, P.24, P.27 and P.28 such as FIR with complaint, wound certificates, IMV report, Spot panchanama, spot sketch, Notice under Sec.133 of M.V.Act, reply notice, Chargesheet, MLC register extracts and police intimations.

PWs 1 and 2 being the injured persons, in their affidavit evidence have deposed about the manner in which they met with an accident and accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MT-6670.

Both the respondents have contended that the  SCCH-1 MVC No.5330/2021 c/w  9 5331/2021 accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and not due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car.
Let us consider the evidence placed by the parties to decide these issues.

11. As per PWs 1 and 2, on 23.10.2021 at about 9.30 am, both were proceeding in a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-S-7770 near Sapotathota,

13 . Exs.P.4 and P.5 which are the spot panchanama and spot sketch reveals the state of affairs at the accident spot.
As per Ex.P.4, the place of accident is near Sapotathota situated on Bhoopasandra main road and the said road is a two way road and on either side of the said road, there are foot paths.

In Ex.P.5, the place of accident Mohan Babu.P vs Chethana.K.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56155141/

As per this document, the driver of the car was moving on Bhoopasandra main road towards  SCCH-1 MVC No.5330/2021 c/w  12 5331/2021 Bhoopasandra, whereas both the motorcycles involved in the accident were moving towards BB road.

Ex.P.5 discloses that the driver of the car who was on the other side of the road has taken it suddenly to the extreme right side and has hit Honda Deo motorcycle and then he has hit the motorcycle of the petitioners, resulting in accident.

Hence, from Exs.P.4 and P.5, it can be safely held that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA- 04-MT-6670 and not on the part of PW.1, as contended by the respondents.
14. IMV report-Ex.P.3 discloses that all the three vehicles involved in the accident were extensively damaged.
The front portion of all the three vehicles were damaged.

Hence, from Ex.P.3, it can be safely held that there was head on collision between the car and the motorcycles,

In the reply notice, the first respondent has stated that on the date of accident, the driver of the car was one Udaykumar and the car was having all the documents and the driver was having DL.
 15.
Wound Certificates-Exs.P.2 and P.13 discloses that in the accident, the petitioners have sustained grievous injuries.

Ex. P.23, P.24, P.27 and P.28 which are the MLC register extracts and police intimations clearly disclose that immediately after the accident, the petitioners were admitted to Bowring Hospital, wherein they have been given treatment.
Chargesheet-Ex.P.8 discloses that the police after detailed investigation, have filed it against one Uday Y.M.
Even as per the chargesheet, it is the driver of the car who has hit the two motorcycles by driving it in a rash and negligent manner.
Thus, all these documents satisfactorily establish the case of the petitioners.

Though the respondents have contended that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent act on the part of  SCCH-1 MVC No.5330/2021 c/w  14 5331/2021 PW.1, but no cogent evidence has been placed by them to prove the said contention.

challenging the chargesheet itself is sufficient to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.
The entire evidence placed by the petitioners remained unrebutted.

Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioners have proved that they met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MT-6670, whereas the second respondent has failed to prove that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle i.e., PW.1.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the Negative.
16. Issue No.2 in MVC No.5330/2021 :

(c) Loss of Income during treatment period :
 PW.1 has deposed that he was a practicing advocate at Lalith Law Firms, Bengaluru and he was earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- per month, but due to the accident, he lost his earnings.

Such being the case, the notional income of PW.1 is taken at Rs.25,000/- per month by considering his avocation as an advocate.
The injury sustained by the petitioner requires minimum three months treatment.

The petitioner herein is a practicing advocate and as he has continued his practice in Civil Courts and Family Courts, I am of the opinion that the profession of an advocate cannot be considered as an employment to apply the ratio laid down in the first decision.

per month as a professor in General Medicine at Varun Arjun Medical College.
PW.2 is relying upon Ex.P.16-bank pass book to show that his salary from Varun Arjun Medical College was credited to his bank account.

and not Rs.15,48,610/- as stated by PW.2 in his chief- examination.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Both the respondents have contended that the  SCCH-1 MVC No.5330/2021 c/w  9 5331/2021 accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and not due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car.
Thus, all these documents satisfactorily establish the case of the petitioners.
Even they have not chosen to examine the driver of the car to disprove the case of the petitioners.
The conduct of the driver of the car in not Mohan Babu.P vs Chethana.K.R on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56155141/
11
challenging the chargesheet itself is sufficient to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.
The entire evidence placed by the petitioners remained unrebutted.
Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioners have proved that they met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MT-6670, whereas the second respondent has failed to prove that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle i.e., PW.1.
Such being the case, the notional income of PW.1 is taken at Rs.25,000/- per month by considering his avocation as an advocate.
The injury sustained by the petitioner requires minimum three months treatment.
During the treatment period, the petitioner was unable to do any work.
From this version of PW.1, it is clear that even after the accident, he has continued his profession and he is getting income.
As such, it can be said that the policy was valid as on the date of accident.

The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Original judgment shall be kept in MVC No.5330/2021 and its copy in another case.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
